xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4330: Optional overdeck.ai sign-in client: pan account login, status and logout

plan.title: Optional overdeck.ai sign-in client: pan account login, status and logout
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The real code surface is four areas (services/account, src/lib/account, src/cli/commands/account, their tests) and 24 files. The subsystem count reaches 9 only because the lint treats each root-level doc file (docs.json, anywhere.mdx, cli/account.mdx, docs/ACCOUNT-SERVICE.md) and the operator hand-off fallback draft as its own subsystem. The three verbs share one token store and one client, so splitting them into sibling issues would ship a verb group missing login or logout.

narratives.Problem: PAN-4293 built the overdeck.ai account service (services/account) but no machine can sign in to it, it is not deployed, and AccountRpc.verifyDevice does not return the GitHub login that the directory (PAN-2356) and Shared Sessions need. There is no pan account verb.
narratives.Proposal: Add githubLogin to the ok branch of AccountRpc.verifyDevice. Build a light client under src/lib/account (token store at ${OVERDECK_HOME}/account.json, 0600, atomic; RFC 8628 device-flow client honoring slow_down and 429) and three light CLI verbs pan account login|status|logout registered as an on-demand command group. Document them in cli/account.mdx and docs/ACCOUNT-SERVICE.md. Hand the deploy (OAuth app, D1, DNS, wrangler deploy) to the operator through a checklist comment on PAN-4330 after proving the Worker bundle builds. Full detail, decisions D-1..D-14 and exact strings live in .pan/drafts/PAN-4330.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Deploying services/account, creating the GitHub OAuth app, the D1 database or DNS (operator-only; agents run only wrangler dev --local, local migrations and deploy --dry-run)
- The PKCE loopback flow, any /api/account/* dashboard route, Settings → Anywhere account panel, the first-run 'Continue from another machine' card
- pan account devices / revoke, pan vault setup --hosted, the hosted vault (PAN-4297), billing (PAN-4294)
- Directory registration (W-LINK5, PAN-2356) or any other reader of the token file
- Any change under services/share/ (githubLogin stays optional there on purpose)
- Any change to the /oauth/token response shape
- Browser auto-open, a pan-account wrapper skill, telemetry changes
- Printing, logging or returning the device token in any output, including --json

autoDecisions.summary: Scope is W-LINK4 only (githubLogin, pan account login|status|logout, operator deploy hand-off); the old body's PKCE dashboard flow, Settings → Anywhere, first-run card, devices/revoke and vault --hosted are non-goals.
autoDecisions.rationale: The rewritten issue body says it owns W-LINK4 and marks the old body 'kept for history'; the 2026-09-30 comment about the first-run card predates the revision-5 rewrite, so this is supersession, not a contradiction.

autoDecisions.summary: Device flow is the only login flow; no --device-code flag.
autoDecisions.rationale: The parent PRD's W-LINK4 names the device flow; PKCE needs a dashboard callback route, which is out of scope.

autoDecisions.summary: Base URL precedence for login: --base-url, then OVERDECK_ACCOUNT_URL, then https://account.overdeck.ai; https required except loopback http; status and logout use the base URL stored in the token file.
autoDecisions.rationale: Lets agents and the operator test against wrangler dev --local, while a token is always used against the service that issued it.

autoDecisions.summary: Login calls GET /v1/me after the token arrives and caches githubLogin and githubId in account.json.
autoDecisions.rationale: The /oauth/token response carries no login (device-flow.ts exchangeDeviceCode), and the done-when requires showing the GitHub login.

autoDecisions.summary: pan account status exits 0 when not signed in; exits 1 on an invalid token or an unreachable service.
autoDecisions.rationale: Sign-in is optional (parent NFR-8), matching pan vault status when the vault is off; real failures still exit non-zero for scripts.

autoDecisions.summary: Logout deletes the local token file even when the server revoke fails, and then exits 1 with a warning.
autoDecisions.rationale: The user asked to sign out; keeping a token they meant to drop is worse than an unrevoked server row they can revoke from another machine.

autoDecisions.summary: Documentation is a new cli/account.mdx plus edits to docs.json, docs/ACCOUNT-SERVICE.md and anywhere.mdx, despite the issue's 'Docs: None'.
autoDecisions.rationale: A new CLI verb and a changed RPC contract are documented surfaces; the finalize docs gate requires a docs item.

autoDecisions.summary: The import-graph guard extends ENTRY_DIRS in the existing tests/unit/lib/vault/import-graph.test.ts instead of adding a new test file.
autoDecisions.rationale: A new walker file with readFileSync fails lint:source-introspection, and importing a .test.ts re-registers its suites.

items.title: Return githubLogin from AccountRpc.verifyDevice

narrative.Action: PRD W-1. In services/account/src/contract.ts add `githubLogin: string` to the ok:true branch of VerifyResult (after githubId). In services/account/src/devices.ts verifyDeviceToken, destructure githubLogin from found.auth and include it in the returned object. In tests/unit/services/account/devices.test.ts update the toEqual at the 'ok: true carries the grant's storage cap' test to include githubLogin: 'user100' (seedUser sets github_login to `user${githubId}`), and add a test that updates users.github_login and asserts verifyDeviceToken returns the new login. Do not touch services/share/.

items.title: Given a seeded user with github id 100, verifyDeviceToken returns { ok: true, userId, githubId: 100, githubLogin: 'user100', deviceId, entitlement }
When the users row's github_login changes to a new value, the next verifyDeviceToken call returns the new login
npm run typecheck:account exits 0 and git diff main -- services/share shows no changes
Token store at ${OVERDECK_HOME}/account.json (src/lib/account/store.ts)

narrative.Action: PRD W-2 and D-6. Create src/lib/account/store.ts exporting ACCOUNT_FILENAME, AccountRecord ({ v: 1, baseUrl, accessToken, deviceId, label, githubLogin: string|null, githubId: number|null, signedInAt }), accountPath(), readAccount() (null on ENOENT, throws 'Cannot read <path>: <reason>. Delete it to sign out locally.' on unreadable/non-JSON/wrong shape; accessToken must match /^odd_[0-9a-f]{64}$/), writeAccount(record) (mkdir -p OVERDECK_HOME, write a temp file with a randomUUID suffix in the same directory with mode 0o600, then rename), removeAccount() (true if removed, false on ENOENT). Imports only node:* and ../paths.js; the module header states that rule (copy the wording style of src/lib/environment-identity.ts). Tests use a temp OVERDECK_HOME per test; the file-mode assertion branches on process.platform (no skipIf).

items.title: writeAccount then readAccount returns an identical record, and on POSIX the file mode is 0o600
Given account.json contains invalid JSON or a token not matching odd_ + 64 hex, readAccount throws an Error whose message contains the file path and 'Delete it to sign out locally'
After writeAccount the directory contains no leftover temp file, and removeAccount returns false when no file exists
Account service HTTP client with RFC 8628 polling (src/lib/account/client.ts)

narrative.Action: PRD W-3 with D-2, D-3, D-5. Create src/lib/account/client.ts exporting DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_BASE_URL ('https://account.overdeck.ai'), resolveBaseUrl(flag, env) (precedence flag > OVERDECK_ACCOUNT_URL > default; https only, http only for 127.0.0.1/localhost/[::1]; no path other than '/', no query, no fragment; else throw AccountClientError('Invalid account service URL: <url>')), platformString(platform, arch) (null unless it matches ^(linux|darwin|win32)-(x64|arm64)$), requestDeviceCode, pollForToken, getMe, revokeDevice, AccountClientError, with the exact signatures in the PRD. Every function takes an optional injected fetch. Poll rules exactly as D-5 (wait `interval` before the FIRST poll, per RFC 8628 §3.4; pending → wait interval; slow_down → use response interval or interval+5; 429 → Retry-After seconds or interval; access_denied/expired_token → terminal reasons; thrown fetch or 5xx retried, three in a row → 'unreachable'; local expiry after expiresIn). Waits are setTimeout promises. Read services/account/src/api.ts for the /v1/me JSON before typing Me. No error message may contain the token. Imports only node:*. Tests use vi.useFakeTimers() and vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync; never real waits; never AbortSignal.timeout.

items.title: Given scripted answers pending, pending, token, pollForToken waits one interval before its first poll and resolves ok only after three intervals of fake time, and a slow_down with interval 10 sends no poll before 10 seconds elapse

Given a 429 with Retry-After: 7, the client waits 7 seconds of fake time before polling again, and access_denied, expired_token and three consecutive thrown fetches each returns reason access_denied, expired_token and unreachable respectively
resolveBaseUrl returns the flag over OVERDECK_ACCOUNT_URL over the default, accepts http://127.0.0.1:8787, and rejects http://example.com, a URL with a path and a URL with a query
platformString('freebsd', 'x64') returns null, and getMe maps a 401 {error:'device_revoked'} to { ok: false, kind: 'unauthorized', error: 'device_revoked' }
pan account login verb (device flow, /v1/me, token file)

expected_outputs: tests/unit/cli/account/login.test.ts passes including the in-process end-to-end test

narrative.Action: PRD W-4 with D-1, D-4, D-7, D-8. Create src/cli/commands/account/shared.ts with AccountIo { out(line), err(line), exit(code): Promise<never> } and defaultAccountIo (console + exitCli from ../../exit.js); do not import src/cli/commands/vault/shared.ts. Create login.ts exporting loginCommand(options: { baseUrl?: string }, io = defaultAccountIo, deps: { fetch?: typeof fetch } = {}): resolveBaseUrl → platformString (unsupported → exit 1 with the D-3 message, no network) → ensureEnvironmentIdentity() (throw → print message, exit 1) → if readAccount() returns a record print the D-7 'Already signed in as …' line → requestDeviceCode → print the four lines from the PRD (verification_uri from the response, never a hardcoded host) → pollForToken → getMe → writeAccount (githubLogin/githubId null and exit 1 with the D-8 message when getMe fails) → print 'Signed in to <baseUrl> as <githubLogin> (device <label>, <deviceId>).'. Tests: (a) end to end through the real account service: injected fetch routes TEST_BASE_URL requests to handle() from services/account/src/routes.ts with makeEnv()/makeDeps({ fetch: githubMock({ identity: OWNER }).fetch }) from tests/unit/services/account/helpers; copy approveInBrowser from tests/unit/services/account/device-flow.test.ts; drive time with fake timers; (b) non-allowlisted identity → invite message, exit 1, no file; (c) unsupported platform → exit 1, zero fetch calls; (d) no output line contains 'odd_'. Reuse captureIo/runCli from tests/unit/cli/vault/helpers.ts. CLOCK RULE for test (a): the service's makeDeps() clock is static (it moves only via deps.clock.advance), while the client's waits run on vi fake timers, so a static server clock answers every poll after the first with slow_down. Build the service deps as makeDeps({ now: Date.now(), fetch: githubMock(...).fetch }) and then override deps.now = () => Date.now() (fake timers mock Date, so client and server share one clock), or call deps.clock.advance(ms) in lockstep with each vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(ms). Expected sequence: request code → approveInBrowser → advance 5 s → one poll → token.

items.title: Given an allowlisted GitHub identity, when the in-process device flow is approved, loginCommand stores a 0600 account.json with an odd_ token and githubLogin 'owner' and prints a line containing 'as owner'
Given a non-allowlisted GitHub identity, loginCommand exits 1 with the invite-list message and creates no account.json
Given platform freebsd-x64, loginCommand exits 1 with the unsupported-platform message and the injected fetch receives zero calls
No captured stdout or stderr line from any login test contains the substring 'odd_'
pan account status verb (human and --json)

narrative.Action: PRD W-5 with D-9. Create src/cli/commands/account/status.ts exporting statusCommand(options: { json?: boolean }, io = defaultAccountIo, deps = {}). No file → 'Not signed in. Run: pan account login', exit 0 (JSON {"signedIn": false}). Otherwise getMe against the stored baseUrl: ok → the four human lines in the PRD (Access: active, or 'expired on <date>; ask the operator to renew the invite.' for grant_expired), exit 0; unauthorized → "This machine's sign-in is no longer valid (<error>). Run: pan account login", exit 1, file kept; unreachable → cached login plus '(account service unreachable: <reason>)', exit 1. --json prints { signedIn, baseUrl, githubLogin, githubId, deviceId, label, access, reachable } and never accessToken. A corrupt token file → the store's error message, exit 1.

items.title: Given no account.json, statusCommand prints 'Not signed in. Run: pan account login' and exits 0
Given a stored token and a 200 /v1/me, statusCommand prints 'Signed in as <login>' and exits 0; with --json the output contains signedIn true and does not contain accessToken or 'odd_'
Given /v1/me returns 401 device_revoked, statusCommand exits 1 with the 'no longer valid (device_revoked)' message and account.json still exists
Given fetch throws, statusCommand prints the cached login with 'account service unreachable' and exits 1
pan account logout verb (server revoke, local delete)

narrative.Action: PRD W-6 with D-10. Create src/cli/commands/account/logout.ts exporting logoutCommand(options: Record<string, never> = {}, io = defaultAccountIo, deps = {}). No file → 'Not signed in.', exit 0, no fetch. Otherwise revokeDevice(baseUrl, token, deviceId): 204/401/404 → removeAccount, print 'Signed out. This machine's device token was revoked.', exit 0; network error or 5xx → removeAccount, stderr 'Signed out locally, but could not revoke the device on <baseUrl>: <reason>. Revoke it from another signed-in machine or ask the operator.', exit 1. Deletes nothing but account.json. Test pre-creates OVERDECK_HOME/vault/key and environment-id.json and asserts they are byte-identical after logout.

items.title: Given a stored token, when DELETE /v1/devices/<deviceId> returns 204, 401 or 404, logoutCommand deletes account.json, prints 'Signed out.' and exits 0
Given fetch throws, logoutCommand deletes account.json, prints the 'Signed out locally, but could not revoke' warning to stderr and exits 1
After logout, pre-existing OVERDECK_HOME/vault/key and environment-id.json are byte-identical, and with no account.json logout prints 'Not signed in.' and makes zero fetch calls

Create src/cli/commands/account/index.ts exporting registerAccountCommands(program) with the exact command/option/description text in the PRD, using an accountAction helper copied from vaultAction in src/cli/commands/vault/index.ts (drops Commander's trailing Command argument) and lazyAction imports of ./login.js, ./status.js, ./logout.js. items.title: When argv is ['account','login','--base-url','http://127.0.0.1:8787'], the parser routes to loginCommand with { baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:8787' }, and ['account','status','--json'] routes to statusCommand with { json: true }

Create cli/account.mdx (frontmatter title 'pan account', description) following cli/devices.mdx: purpose (optional sign-in for the directory and hosted features), login (device flow, printed URLs, --base-url, OVERDECK_ACCOUNT_URL, invite-only message), status (fields, --json, exit codes per D-9), logout (server revoke + local delete, never touches vault or environment-id.json, the offline case per D-10), where the token lives (${OVERDECK_HOME}/account.json, 0600) and what the account never holds (vault key, passphrase, conversation content). expected_outputs: build:dry exits 0 with no Cloudflare credentials
issue 4330 shows the deploy checklist comment

narrative.Action: PRD W-10. The work agent never deploys and never runs wrangler login, d1 create, remote migrations, secret put or wrangler deploy. Run `npm --prefix services/account run build:dry` (must exit 0) and `npm run typecheck:account`. Write the checklist to a temp file in the scratch area and post it with `gh issue comment 4330 --body-file <file>`: the eight Deploy steps from docs/ACCOUNT-SERVICE.md (OAuth app with callback https://account.overdeck.ai/auth/github/callback; npx wrangler login; npx wrangler d1 create overdeck-account and commit the database_id into services/account/wrangler.jsonc; npx wrangler d1 migrations apply overdeck-account --remote; secrets GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET, OWNER_GITHUB_ID; npx wrangler deploy; smoke test curl https://account.overdeck.ai/healthz shows configured:true; rollback npx wrangler rollback), then the post-deploy acceptance check (fresh OVERDECK_HOME: pan account login → approve at the printed URL → pan account status prints 'Signed in as <login>' → pan account logout prints 'Signed out.'). Then run pan tell flywheel-orchestrator "work PAN-4330: account service deploy needs the operator (OAuth app, D1, DNS); checklist posted on #4330" (sandbox disabled). Implementation checkpoint: if gh issue comment fails, commit the same text to .pan/drafts/pan-4330-deploy-handoff.md and name that path in the PR body. readiness is sequential because it must run once, after the shipped verbs and RPC change exist.
